newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 42,600 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 43.737 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 19,500 tonnes, in Denmark 10,000, in the Netherlands 8,100 and in the U.K. 5,000 tonnes, it added.

This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.777 million tonnes. This compares with the 111,250 tonnes awarded on March 27, 1996, when the cumulative tonnage totalled 1.834 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the maximum subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 43.737 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast the total authorised sugar tonnage export awards to be between 30,000 and 60,000 tonnes versus 54,500 last week when the restitution was 44.329 Ecus.
